answer: Pay agents for forecasts that resolve months later, like whether a shifting dune will close a tidal inlet by spring, or what an opal lot fetches at auction. Each seat earns only the log-score gain its forecast adds to the crowd average once the outcome is known, and that pay stays locked until then. A clone farm files near-identical forecasts, so each copy adds almost nothing over its siblings while every copy ties up stake for months; spreading them apart to look distinct just makes most of them wrong.
